messages:
amy_cs: Heads-up — onboarding call with Alex @ Acme this morning. They got everything wired but are seeing an onboarding surge of 429s right after app start. Reported from the browser embed (v0.9.2) and our Node SDK (v1.4.0). They say initial few requests succeed, then a flurry of preflight/auth failures and 429s when many users hit the page at once.

amy_cs: Alex pasted a capture: `401` on `/v1/auth/preflight` then a bunch of `429` on `/v1/generate` within 10s of a deploy. They use ephemeral tokens with a refresh endpoint on their backend.

amy_cs: I asked for logs, but wanted to loop in eng — Jordan can you advise quick triage steps? I'm marked this as "onboard at risk" until we stabilize. :warning:

jordan_eng: Thanks — tagging in. Two quick hypotheses: 1) client preflight fanout (many tabs) is racing token refresh and reusing tokens, causing handshake thrash; 2) backend token endpoint overloaded and returning stale/401, leading clients to retry aggressively -> 429.

jordan_eng: Can you ask Alex for a minimal repro steps + a HAR or SDK debug log? Specifically we need the sequence: preflight -> token fetch -> generate. Also ask them to enable `RW_SDK_DEBUG=true` in env for 1 minute to get full traces.

amy_cs: Asked for HAR and enabled debug instructions. Alex replied with a short log snippet:
```
[09:12:01] GET /v1/auth/preflight 200 (ok) tx=abcd
[09:12:02] POST /v1/auth/token 200 ttl=15s token=ephemeral_... tx=ef01
[09:12:05] POST /v1/generate 200 tx=g1
[09:12:05] POST /v1/generate 429 retry-after=1s tx=g2
[09:12:06] POST /v1/generate 429 retry-after=1s tx=g3
[09:12:07] POST /v1/auth/token 401 tx=ef02
[09:12:07] POST /v1/generate 429 tx=g4
```

amy_cs: They said this happens when their dev team deploys and users refresh simultaneously.

ops_oncall: Quick checks: look at our ingress rate headers and auth service logs for tx ef02. Jordan, can you grep `auth-service` for that trace id? Could be token minting rate-limit.

jordan_eng: On it. Running a quick query now.

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: `acme/web-frontend` deployed by @alex.acme at 2024-04-03T09:11:50Z.

jordan_eng: Found related auth logs: many short-lived token requests from same client fingerprint; auth-service returned 429s then 401s when internal cache miss collided with quota. Root cause looks like preflight endpoint returned ok, but token endpoint hit a per-API-key mint rate cap during bursts. We also saw client using TTL=15s which is very short for many tabs.

jordan_eng: Immediate mitigations we can recommend to the customer:
- increase ephemeral token TTL on their backend to 60s (or reuse tokens across tabs)
- add jittered backoff and cap concurrent in-flight `POST /v1/auth/token` requests per session (e.g., single inflight token request per browser session)
- implement client-side debounce on initial preflight/token calls (stagger on page load)

amy_cs: Noted. I can push those to Alex as short-term fixes. Any server-side knobs we can open quickly?

jordan_eng: We can temporarily bump their token mint quota for the org for 24h while they roll out fixes. I can make a one-off change if ops_oncall approves. Also can increase grace window on our token validation to accept tokens minted within last 2s to tolerate races.

ops_oncall: Approve temporary quota bump + 2s validation grace. I'll coordinate with infra to apply and monitor. Please capture the exact org id and a time window.

amy_cs: I'll get Alex to send the org id and confirm a maintenance window. I'll also send them a short snippet they can paste into the frontend to debounce:

```
// pseudo: single inflight token fetch
let tokenPromise = null;
function fetchEphemeralToken() {
  if (tokenPromise) return tokenPromise;
  tokenPromise = fetch('/internal/getToken').finally(() => setTimeout(() => { tokenPromise = null }, 1000));
  return tokenPromise;
}
```

amy_cs: Alex said they'll try the debounce + TTL increase and asked if we can monitor for 2 hours after.

jordan_eng: I'll open a debug window on our side and watch auth-service + gateway metrics for that org. If we still see >5% 429 ratio after changes, we'll escalate to mitigation plan B (sticky token cache + extended TTL on our gateway).

amy_cs: Plan to schedule a 30m screen-share at 11:00 PST to help them apply fixes. Alex is available.

amy_cs: TL;DR for ticket: onboarding customer (Acme) hit preflight/token fanout -> token mint rate cap -> client retries -> 429 cascade. Short-term: TTL increase, debounce single inflight token, temporary quota bump. Ops approved. Follow-up: monitor 2h post-fix, escalate if >5% 429.

amy_cs: Adding note to the account health doc and setting renewal risk to "watch" until stable. :white_check_mark:
